::: {.landing-bio}
Jacob Wallace is an Associate Professor of Public Health (Health Policy) at the Yale School of Public Health and a Faculty Research Fellow at the National Bureau of Economic Research.

Professor Wallace is a health economist who conducts rigorous empirical research to inform US health care policy. In his academic research, he studies the economics of public insurance markets, with a focus on Medicaid. He uses randomized and quasi-experimental designs, often in partnership with state governments, to study managed care procurement, benefit administration, and the value of public insurance.

Wallace's research has been published in leading economics and clinical journals---including the *American Economic Review* and the *New England Journal of Medicine*---and received the Willard G. Manning Award for the Best Research in Health Econometrics and the Outstanding Statistical Application Award from the American Statistical Association. His research has also been widely covered by media, including the *New York Times*, *Washington Post*, and *NPR*.

Before academia, Wallace served as a Medicaid policy analyst for New York State, worked as a
data scientist in Silicon Valley, and co-founded the advocacy organization Young Invincibles.
He holds degrees from Swarthmore College and Harvard University.

:::

```{r}
#| echo: false

source("R/substack.R")
posts <- yaml::read_yaml("data/substack_posts.yml")
if (length(posts) > 0) {
  cat("## Latest writing\n\n")
  for (p in head(posts, 3)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      '<div class="post"><div class="meta">%s · %s</div><div class="headline"><a href="%s">%s</a></div></div>\n',
      html_escape(p$date), toupper(p$source), html_escape(p$url), html_escape(p$title)))
  }
  cat('\n[All writing →](writing.qmd)\n')
}
```
